page.layout: One printed page: running head at top centre; page number top left; heading across full width below running head; a woodcut emblem (tree with figures and banners) centred; verse in italic lines below the woodcut; catchword "Quaesi-" at lower right.

main_text.head: ARBOR MALOS MALA FERT, fructus, bona sed bonos.
main_text.p: [Woodcut emblem: a tree bearing banners inscribed Vis, Luxuria, Philarguria, Philutimia, Curiositas, Superbia, Invidia, and a banner reading "Dic quibus in terris, nec eris mihi parvus Apollo"; figures of clergy seated beneath the tree, a skeleton and a devil in the branches.]
main_text.l: Dic quibus in terris, & eris mihi magnus Apollo,
Est etiam in sanctis labes, nec dicere quicquam
Est pura à naevis mens mea tota, potest.

page.notes: The woodcut banners read: Vis (top); Philutimia (left), Luxuria (centre), Philargyria (right); Curiositas, Superbia, Invidia (middle row); the scroll across the tree reads "Dic quibus in terris ! nec eris mihi parvus Apollo" with partly obscured letters. The running head "EMBLEMA" is set in spaced capitals. Some letters in the banners and the scroll are doubtful and are not marked individually; the woodcut captions are not transcribed exactly.
